questions.question: The term Renaissance refers to a renewed interest in which cultural heritage?
choices: Industrial factory systems
Classical Greek and Roman learning
Modern international law
Viking maritime law

questions.question: Which region was a major early center of the European Renaissance?
choices: The Italian peninsula
The Scandinavian peninsula
The Russian steppe
The Scottish Highlands

questions.question: What was Renaissance humanism?
choices: A rejection of every form of religion
A requirement that rulers abandon education
A movement to end the study of ancient languages
An approach emphasizing classical texts and human capabilities

questions.question: Which family was especially associated with patronage in Florence?
choices: Romanov
Habsburg
Medici
Tudor

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
choices: Leonardo da Vinci
Michelangelo
Raphael
Donatello

questions.question: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
choices: Petrarch
Michelangelo
Botticelli
Erasmus

questions.question: What is linear perspective in painting?
choices: Using only written words to represent a scene
Giving every object the same apparent size
Creating an illusion of depth with converging lines
Removing all recognizable objects from an image

questions.question: Why did wealthy merchants support Renaissance art?
choices: Art patronage was available only to peasants
Artists were prohibited from accepting church commissions
Paintings replaced currency in every Italian market
Patronage could express wealth, status, faith, and civic pride

questions.question: Why were Italian city-states well placed to support cultural innovation?
choices: Trade and banking helped concentrate wealth in urban centers
They had no contact with neighboring regions
Their economies depended entirely on isolated subsistence farms
They were all governed by one elected national parliament

questions.question: How did printing with movable type affect Renaissance learning in Europe?
choices: It restricted books to handwritten copies
It increased the availability and circulation of texts
It removed the need for readers to understand languages
It immediately made literacy universal

questions.question: Why is it misleading to say Renaissance art was entirely nonreligious?
choices: Renaissance artists never studied human anatomy
The period had no churches commissioning art
Every Renaissance painting depicted a pagan ruler
Many works still depicted Christian subjects and served religious patrons

questions.question: How did Northern Renaissance humanists such as Erasmus often use classical learning?
choices: To organize industrial labor unions
To prohibit the printing of religious texts
To examine religious practice and encourage reform
To replace every European language with Greek

questions.question: What was a major concern of Machiavelli's The Prince?
choices: How rulers acquire and maintain political power
How farmers predict annual rainfall
How artists mix pigments for murals
How sailors calculate ocean depth

questions.question: Why did some writers use vernacular languages rather than Latin?
choices: To stop people from reading their works
To reach readers in languages used in everyday life
To ensure that only ancient Romans could understand them
To avoid every form of local cultural expression

questions.question: What does Leonardo's work in both art and anatomy suggest about Renaissance inquiry?
choices: Science and art were legally required to remain separate
Artists avoided observing the natural world
Painting had replaced all other fields of knowledge
Observation could connect artistic practice with scientific investigation

questions.question: A painting makes distant buildings appear smaller and uses a vanishing point. Which technique is being applied?
choices: Manuscript illumination
Relief carving
Linear perspective
Woodblock text printing

questions.question: A historian studies a commission paid for by a banker. Which question best examines the patron's influence?
choices: How did the banker's goals shape the work's subject and display?
How did the painting's later sale price compare with its original cost?
How did the artist's materials compare with those used by sculptors?
How did the painting's frame change during later restoration?

questions.question: Which comparison best describes Renaissance culture's relationship with the Middle Ages?
choices: It arose without any earlier European learning
It introduced changes while retaining important religious and cultural continuities
It ended all religious institutions immediately
It restored the Roman Empire's original government across Europe

questions.question: A student claims humanism meant all humanists rejected Christianity. Which evidence would best challenge the claim?
choices: A list of merchants who financed Florentine building projects
A map showing trade routes between northern Italian cities
A humanist's text using classical learning to discuss Christian ethics
An inventory of imported pigments in a painter's workshop

questions.question: Two cities have different artistic styles despite sharing classical influences. What is the strongest conclusion?
choices: One city must not belong to the Renaissance
Classical influences required identical artwork everywhere
Trade had no influence on artistic development
Renaissance ideas were adapted to different local conditions
